why: Focused checks are required for tests and correctness because this changes SQL boolean simplification logic, including three-valued null semantics and nondeterministic expressions; performance and backward-compatibility checks are also warranted for a new bounded rewrite that changes observable plans. The user-visible simplification warrants a meaningful change description and user-value/least-surprise review.

Required checks include correctness, tests, backward compatibility, spec conformance, error behavior, and documentation because OFFSET expression support changes parsing, validation, execution, and generated SQL across multiple adapters. User value and least-surprise behavior also merit focused review since this is a user-visible SQL feature with potentially observable differences in expression evaluation and dialect support.

Tests, correctness, and spec conformance are required because the optimizer transformation must preserve aggregate semantics, including the empty-input/global-aggregate case. Backward compatibility is required because the rule's applicability changes for existing plans, so verify it avoids regressions while retaining valid transformations.

Focused checks are required for correctness, tests, public behavioral compatibility, error reporting, and the new API contract; the test fixture appears to construct its intended two-column mismatch from the one-column input instead. The new validity behavior may reject previously accepted plans, and the PR description provides no rationale or release note for that user-visible change.

Tests, backward_compat, error_model, correctness, surprising_behavior, and contradictions warrant focused checks because the fix changes overload resolution for existing SQL calls and claims to prevent spurious validation errors; inspect the regression test and mapped-kind comparison for edge cases and consistency with the PR description. The change is cohesive and can be reviewed by one person.

Focused checks are required for tests, security, backward compatibility, correctness, surprising behavior, contradictions, and spec conformance because the PR changes escaping of string literals sent to Pig, affecting generated queries and escaping semantics. The added cases should be checked against Pig's actual parsing behavior and the intended compatibility change.

Tests, correctness, and performance require focused review because this adds a complex join algorithm and planner rule with sorting, scanning, and residual-condition handling. Backward compatibility, concurrency, user value, surprising behavior, and contradictions also merit focused checks because the new rule is registered in default planning and introduces observable execution and type/null semantics.

Focused checks are owed for tests, correctness, backward compatibility, surprising behavior, and contradictions: the rewrite changes where outer ORDER BY/OFFSET/FETCH land, with new regression coverage but potentially altered handling of existing limits. The PR claims preservation, so reviewers should verify that intended query semantics survive both select and WITH rewrites.

Tests and correctness require focused review because the validator rewrite changes ORDER BY resolution and aggregate matching across join types; backward compatibility, user value, and spec conformance also merit checks because common-column semantics are externally observable. Contradictions deserves attention because the PR changes implementation and comments together, while the scope of the description and any documentation obligations should be verified.

Tests is required because this PR re-enables behavior tests, so their assertions and coverage must be checked; correctness merits attention to ensure updated expectations match the current query and metadata behavior.

Tests, backward compatibility, and correctness are required because the change alters validator handling of common columns in USING/NATURAL JOIN queries when identifier expansion is disabled, and the regression coverage must verify that behavior.

Focused review is owed for tests, user docs, comments, change description, security, compatibility, correctness, user value, surprising behavior, contradictions, and spec conformance: the PR changes literal and identifier escaping across multiple dialects/adapters, adds a configurable fallback behavior, and introduces a broad behavioral surface with significant claims in comments and description.

Required checks include tests, user documentation, security, backward compatibility, correctness, user value, surprising behavior, contradictions, and build/CI: the PR changes compilation defaults and CI JDK provisioning, adds a toolchain resolver, and claims unchanged runtime/test coverage that should be verified.

Required checks cover changed skip/mark/reset semantics and error handling, regression tests, and public behavioral compatibility with InputStream contracts. Performance and doc comments also merit focused review because the PR adds a seek-based hot-path optimization and changes documented contracts.

Correctness, user value, and least-astonishment checks are required because this PR changes many user-visible translations, including a suspicious fuzzy entry and potentially misleading technical terminology. Backward compatibility and contradiction checks are required to ensure generated catalog behavior, fuzzy handling, metadata, and the stated scope agree with the actual PO and Java outputs.

Focused review is owed for tests, user docs and release/change description because this user-visible redirect behavior needs validation and a changelog/documentation check; backward compatibility and user value are central to whether the legacy URL mappings work as intended. Correctness and contradictions merit checking the claimed 436 aliases for omissions, collisions, and valid destinations, including the stated Hugo output.

Focused checks are required for tests, security, correctness, surprising behavior, contradictions, and build_ci: the workflow commits and conditionally uses a coverage token, changes dynamic matrix/report/failure behavior, and couples Codecov notification finalization to all matrix jobs. The split CI/security and workflow-correctness concerns warrant independent review.

Tests, error_model, and correctness need focused attention because this fixes a concrete close/flush failure path, and reviewers should verify flushing works before closure, including failure behavior and regression coverage.

Focused checks are owed for tests, backward compatibility, error behavior, correctness, and contradictions because this changes cache invalidation across server versions and adds a regression test for the resulting distinct error/reprepare paths. Docs and comments are touched and merit a glance for version-specific claims.

User-visible connection-property additions and behavior changes make user_docs and change_description checks necessary, and the substantial release-note content merits correctness and cross-file contradiction checks. A single reviewer can cover this cohesive documentation-only change, especially to verify that the two versioned changelogs and summaries accurately match the release entries.

Focused checks are required for security, correctness, backward compatibility, error handling, tests, and RFC 5929/spec conformance because the PR changes fail-closed SCRAM channel-binding negotiation and introduces new rejection paths. Contradictions also merits review because the description, remediation message, and implementation must agree about which certificate algorithms support channel binding.

Tests, error_model, and correctness need focused review because the diff only guards one parser entry point and tests only toTimestamp, despite the description claiming coverage of all entry points. Contradictions must also be checked because the submitted diff does not match the described shared guard and comprehensive tests.

Build/CI deserves focused review because the change replaces the pinned checkout action revision across 14 workflows, affecting CI and release execution. A quick check of action compatibility and consistent pin updates is warranted; other touched axes merit only a glance.

Tests is required because this PR adds a regression test for a behavior change and needs verification that it actually exercises the reported issue; correctness is required to check the expected COLUMN_DEF values against PostgreSQL behavior across supported versions.

Required focused review is owed for tests, doc_comments, performance, security, backward_compat, error_model, correctness, user_value, surprising_behavior, contradictions, and spec_conformance: this broad protocol-reader change alters framing, allocation bounds, error handling, and observable connection behavior. Split the review because protocol/security correctness, buffering/resource behavior, and contract/documentation/test coverage are distinct review tasks.

Tests, backward compatibility, correctness, and build/CI need focused checks because this toolchain upgrade can break supported build environments, wrapper integrity, or project configuration. User docs and release notes merit a glance because the change is a build-tool version update.

Required attention is warranted for correctness and regression tests because this modifies non-trivial wildcard/capture substitution and nullability logic; backward compatibility merits focused review because the behavior changes under wildcard handling configuration. The new private non-trivial method requires Javadoc, while the user-visible bug fix needs a clear change description/changelog assessment and related docs/tests should be checked for consistency.

Required axes are correctness, backward compatibility, spec conformance, tests, doc comments, change description, surprising behavior, and contradictions: this changes javac type-copying and wildcard-bound semantics, adds public helper/API contracts, and claims a user-visible nullability fix without checker-level coverage in this PR. The change-description obligation and consistency between the preparatory PR description, comments, and tests also merit focused attention.

Tests, backward compatibility, and correctness need focused review because this fixes behavior by changing cached modeled type-variable bounds from one value per key to multiple values, altering cached data and exposed method types. Contradictions merit a check because the description and regression test claim handling of multiple nullable bounds, while the shown test covers a single BiConsumer declaration.

Required checks cover new anonymous-diamond inference and regressions (tests, correctness, backward compatibility), the changed internal inference contract/comments, user-visible behavior and its description, and consistency across code, tests, and claims. Single review is appropriate for this focused, cohesive change.

Correctness and spec_conformance need focused review because this large AST-based checker classifies many type-use contexts and constructs fixes. Tests, docs/description, compatibility, error behavior, user value, contradictions, and build_ci also warrant focused checks: the PR adds a configurable, user-visible warning with severity and fix behavior, but its description claims disabled-by-default while the shown code declares WARNING.

Focused review is required for tests and correctness because this changes generic type and nullability inference across arrays, conditionals, loops, and method references; backward compatibility and doc-comment/contradiction checks are also warranted because public method signatures change and comments/contracts were revised alongside the resolver behavior.

Tests and correctness are required because this behavior change adds three new method models but includes no corresponding regression tests, and the generic signatures must match supported APIs. The description already explains the user-visible change, so no changelog-level description pass is clearly owed.

Concurrency, correctness, and surprising behavior merit focused review because the new group key is meant to distinguish pull-request, branch-push, and merge-queue runs, and its behavior depends on GitHub event context. Build/CI is required because the workflow trigger configuration changes to add merge-queue CI.

Required checks are owed for tests, build_ci, and spec_conformance because this adds CI validation and configures Renovate-specific behavior; correctness and security merit focused review of the matching, grouping, pinning, and third-party update policy. User-visible automation also requires review of its value, surprising behavior, description, and cross-file contradictions.

Required checks are tests and correctness because the PR changes nontrivial wildcard/type-variable annotation restoration and adds focused regression cases; backward compatibility and surprising behavior merit focused checks because nullability results for existing generic calls change. Doc comments and contradictions are also required to verify the new bounds-handling contracts and consistency among code, tests, and the PR description.

Focused review is owed for correctness and regression-test coverage because this changes contextual wildcard/capture bound resolution across several complex inference cases. Backward compatibility, surprising behavior, and contradictions also merit focused checks because inferred nullness and wildcard containment behavior are user-visible and the PR updates related contracts and regression expectations.
